newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle sales thin at $67 -feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle sales thin at $67 -feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle sold at $67.00 per cwt in a limited test, down $1.00 from Wednesday, feedlot sources said.

About 3,000 slaughter steers and heifers, that will likely grade select and choice, sold in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area. Sales in Kansas also were limited at $67.00 and totalled under 1,000 head as of midday, they said.
The sales brought the Panhandle week-to-date figure close to 73,500 head and Kansas close to 65,000, sources said.
Most cattle owners continued to resist further bids at $67.00 by pricing cattle mostly at $68.00, the sources said.
Fed cattle weakness was attributed to sharp losses in live cattle futures at the Chicago Mercantile Exchange, the feedlot managers said.
Losses were tempered by outlooks for continued firm beef prices, several feedlot managers said.
Beef prices at midday were up $0.06 to $0.47 per cwt, with 149 fabricated loads sold, USDA reported.
There was talk that a number of cattle sold during Wednesday's brief, but hectic trade were picked up early Thursday, which fortified ideas that packers were short on live inventory, sources said.
